learning_outcomes.text: The student identifies and describes basic principles and methods of mechanical engineering applied to the Turbomachinery course.
Knows and can explain the constructive principles and mechanical and thermal schemes of the main types of turbomachinery.
Knows the processes that occur in turbomachinery.
Knows the main characteristics of turbomachinery.
Explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results, technical documentation, and phenomena.
Can compare different turbomachinery based on their technical characteristics.
Highlights the phenomena influencing the operation of turbomachinery.
Understands the characteristic curves of turbomachinery and explains the operating particularities based on these curves.
The student operates with basic methods and techniques from the field of turbomachinery and associates them with specific graphical representations: i-s diagrams, characteristic curves.
The student applies criteria, evaluation methods, concepts, theories, and programs in the design of turbomachinery.
The student selects and applies basic concepts, principles, and methods in the field for thermodynamic calculations specific to different types of turbomachinery.
The student selects and applies criteria, principles, and evaluation methods for identifying, modeling, and experimenting with thermodynamic and thermal phenomena and processes.
The student develops professional projects of medium complexity by selecting, combining, and utilizing concepts, principles, methodologies, and technologies from the field of mechanical engineering.
The student selects and analyzes specific bibliographic sources in the field of turbomachinery.
The student demonstrates autonomy in learning specific issues in the field of turbomachinery.

The student respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making to solve problems; integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels; continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective methods and techniques for lifelong learning.

syllabus_topics: Introduction - Definitions, classifications of turbomachinery, uses of turbomachinery, history, characteristic parameters
Theoretical bases of turbomachinery operation
Continuity equation for steady flow applied to turbomachinery
First Principle of Thermodynamics applied to turbomachinery. Particularizations for apparatus and machines component of turbomachinery
Principle of momentum conservation, impulse theorem applied to turbomachinery. Examples
Braking parameters. State equation in braking parameters
Force generation through the interaction between a moving fluid and a solid body. Action force. Reaction force. Examples
Force generation through the interaction between a moving fluid and the moving blades of the turbine stage. Power exchanged by blades.
Equation of turbomachinery
Nozzles and diffusers in thermal turbomachinery
Physico-mathematical model of the theoretical geometric nozzle. Isentropic flow, representation in thermodynamic diagrams
Theoretical exit velocity from the nozzle. Theoretical flow rate and maximum flow rate through the theoretical geometric nozzle. Graphical representations
Critical parameters of the nozzle. Speed of sound and maximum velocity in the critical section
Convergent, divergent, convergent-divergent nozzles and diffusers. Parameters, construction
Behavior of real nozzles. Geometric nozzle with friction. Processes represented in thermodynamic diagrams
Thermodynamic study of steam and gas turbines. Energetics of the elementary stage
Processes in the impulse turbine stage
Processes in the reaction turbine stage
Losses in steam turbines: in valves, in nozzles, in blades, at exit, due to friction and ventilation, due to internal leakages, humidity, external leakages, mechanical
Efficiencies of the turbine stage / efficiencies of the steam turbine as a whole
Requirements for the construction of impulse moving blades
Requirements for the construction of reaction moving blades
Labyrinth seals. Principle diagram, operation, thermodynamic diagrams
Steam turbine installations
Single-pressure stage impulse turbine (de Laval). Diagram, parameter variation in thermodynamic diagrams, blade profile, velocity triangles
Single-pressure stage, multi-velocity stage impulse turbine (Curtis). Diagram, parameter variation in thermodynamic diagrams, blade profile, velocity triangles
Multi-pressure stage impulse turbine (Rateau). Diagram, parameter variation in thermodynamic diagrams, blade profile, velocity triangles
Multi-pressure stage reaction turbine (Parsons). Diagram, parameter variation in thermodynamic diagrams, blade profile, velocity triangles
Mixed turbine.
Multi-stage centrifugal turbine (Ljungstrom). Diagram, thermodynamic diagrams, velocity triangles
Multi-flow turbines and multi-body turbines
Gas turbine installations
Principle diagram of a stationary Gas Turbine Installation (GTI)
Theoretical cycle of GTI with constant pressure combustion (Brayton). Efficiency
Real cycle of GTI with constant pressure combustion. Possibilities to increase efficiency
Centripetal gas turbine. Diagram, thermodynamic diagrams
Principle diagram of a turbojet engine. Operation
Principle diagram of a turboprop engine. Operation
Principle diagram of a turbofan engine. Operation
Centrifugal dynamic compressors
Construction and operation of a single-stage centrifugal compressor
Representation of the compression process in T-S, p-V, p-path, and i-path diagrams

Thermogasdynamic process in the impeller. Derivation of the expression for total pressure increase when passing through the impeller using the angular momentum theorem. Expression of total pressure increase written as a function of absolute velocity components. Specific mechanical work done by centrifugal forces
Process in the inlet guide vane of the centrifugal compressor. Constructive variants of the impeller. Influence of angle P2p on the total pressure increase in the impeller
Kinematic reaction degree. Definitions
Impeller with a finite number of blades. Force balance. Differential equations of flow through the centrifugal impeller
Axial dynamic compressors
Construction of stationary axial compressors and those used in aviation turbojet engines
Kinematics of the axial stage
Thermodynamic aspects of flow through the axial compressor. Efficiencies, power, specific mechanical work. Expression of specific mechanical work as a function of velocities
Isentropic thermodynamic reaction degree. Kinematic reaction degree
Types of elementary axial stages, with different reaction degrees. Comparison between types of elementary stages for constant MWI and constant u
Characteristic curves of dynamic compressors: flow characteristics; speed characteristics. Universal characteristics
Constructive and functional elements of dynamic compressors
Regulation and automation of dynamic compressor operation
Laboratory: Occupational safety norms in the turbine laboratory.
Laboratory: Determination of the velocity coefficient of nozzles.
Laboratory: Plotting the flow characteristic of the nozzle at constant inlet pressure.
Laboratory: Determination of gasdynamic forces acting on a blade cascade.
Laboratory: Experimental verification of the calculation relation for labyrinth seal losses.
Laboratory: Plotting torque and power characteristics as a function of speed for a single-stage axial turbine.
Laboratory: Plotting the expansion ratio - flow rate characteristic for a single-stage axial turbine (constant n).
Project: Design of a single-stage centrifugal air compressor. Initial data.
Project: Calculations for the inlet guide vane. Representation of the process in the i-s diagram for the inlet guide vane.
Project: Calculations for air flow in the impeller blade zone.
Project: Thermogasdynamic calculation of the smooth and bladed diffuser.
Project: Determination of stage efficiency.
teaching_methods: Classical lectures with exposition and presentation on the board
Drawing schemes, describing physical and mathematical modeling of studied phenomena
Short recap of previous lecture's notions at the beginning of each course
Interactive course, with direct involvement of the audience
assessment_rules: To pass, a minimum grade of 5 is required for each of the course activities (exam, laboratory, project). The final evaluation result is based on the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the course. Grades are awarded from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimal learning outcomes for a course and the awarding of its corresponding study credits.
